scenario: An app uses Android accessibility services to overlay fake login screens on top of legitimate banking apps (a documented 'overlay attack' pattern).

supported_findings: The app registers an accessibility service (OverlayAccessibilityService) combined with SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, capabilities consistent with rendering overlays on top of other apps.
A string references a target package name matching a banking app and a field labeled credential_capture_field, consistent with overlay-based credential capture design.
A single 900-byte connection to collect.example.com occurred, consistent in size with a small captured-credential payload but not confirmed as such from bytes alone.
unsupported_claims_to_watch_for: Any claim that a specific person's banking credentials were captured or that a specific person's bank account was accessed -- no evidence in this case identifies a device user or confirms payload content.
Any claim that the 900-byte transfer definitively contained credentials rather than any other small payload.
Any claim naming the banking app's real institution as having been breached -- only a placeholder target-package string is present.
